sections.html:
Washington sits in the southwest corner of Utah, a short drive east of St. George on Interstate 15, and is part of the St. George metro area. About 37,107 people live here now. The count was 27,993 in 2020 and 18,761 in 2010.

Growth came fast, so the housing is young. Most houses are under twenty-five years old. The streets around the original townsite have a different feel from the planned subdivisions built after 2000, and sellers in old town, Buena Vista, Green Springs or the Washington Fields area in the north will meet different buyers. In 2020 the city had 11,523 housing units, 18.1% of them vacant. Many of those are second homes, which the county water district puts at more than 20% of homes across the county.

Summers are hot and dry. The St. George valley averages a July high of 101.9 degrees, with around 60 afternoons a year over 100, and January lows near 28.4 degrees. Rain adds up to only about 9 inches. The sun does the damage here, and an inspector's list usually starts with:

  • An air conditioner that has run for months every year for a long time.
  • Tile or shingles and the underlayment beneath them.
  • Stucco cracks, faded paint and weathered south-facing decks.
  • Sprinkler lines and pool pumps that give out in extreme heat.

Putting off any of these repairs is a frequent reason a listing stalls. It is also why some owners choose an as-is sale, where the buyer takes the house in its current condition.

Water supply shapes yards in Washington County. The county's population centers draw on the Virgin River basin and use more than 90% of the reliable annual supply, which pushed most cities to adopt turf limits.

New residential lots may have grass on no more than 8% of the lot, with a separate cap for large lots. Grass is banned in park strips, in areas narrower than 8 feet and on slopes. Developers must irrigate with secondary or reuse water where it exists, and watering with drinking water is banned from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. in summer. Heavy users also face an excessive water use fee of $1.00 per 1,000 gallons above a set monthly volume.

Before you rip out or replant a yard, get the city's water conservation form or call city hall about your lot. A large lawn on an older lot costs more to maintain, and buyers notice.

sections.h2: Permits for work you did before listing
sections.html:
Finished work should have a permit on file. Washington City's Building Department issues them for single-family permits, additions, basement finishes, demolition, detached accessory buildings, garages and shops, sheds and patio covers, swimming pools and solar.

  • Permit applications and inspection requests go through the City Inspect portal. A request in by 5 p.m. on a business day is typically handled the next business day.
  • Work hours run 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Concrete crews may start at 3 a.m. from April through October.
  • An accessory dwelling unit may need a deed restriction.
  • The department is at 111 North 100 East, phone (435) 656-6326.

Buyers' inspectors tend to find unpermitted work, a finished basement for example. If you are unsure what an earlier owner did, ask the department before you put up a sign.

sections.h2: Property tax and recording at sale time
sections.html:
Real property tax in this county comes due on November 30. If the bill goes unpaid, the lien attaches to the parcel, so a new owner inherits the problem. Notices are mailed to owners, though a lost one changes nothing, and the Treasurer's Office will send another on request. At closing the settlement statement divides the year's tax between you and the buyer.

Pay part of a bill any time, as long as each payment is $10 or more per parcel. Delinquent accounts do not get installment plans. Each May the county holds a tax sale for parcels that stayed delinquent five years or longer.

Your main home is taxed on 55% of market value, since Utah exempts 45% for residences. That discount disappears for a second home or an empty house, which gets taxed on full value. Moved away? Read the next bill closely.

To record a deed, visit the Washington County Recorder at 111 East Tabernacle Street in St. George. Expect $45.00 per document and $2.00 for every legal description beyond ten. The office stops taking filings at 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time.

Builders put up more than 3,300 homes here between 2017 and 2021, including denser multifamily buildings near Exit 13. Washington has three exits on the interstate, and the area near Exit 10 and Exit 13 has the shopping and the highest traffic. All that new inventory competes with resale houses and weighs on asking prices.

An older house should be priced against nearby resales instead of against the newest builds. Be ready to say what you have updated, such as the roof, the cooling system and the windows.

Three routes exist in Washington: hire an agent, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer. Each balances speed, price and hassle differently. The agent route exposes the house to the most buyers, at the cost of open houses, repair demands and a closing that waits on the buyer's mortgage.

Cash fits a house with deferred repairs, a tight move date, or an inherited Washington County property you would rather hand off. Cash Home Buyers quotes houses in any condition, and requesting a quote obligates you to nothing. With no showings and no lender in the middle, you choose a closing date that suits you.

Sellers here keep hitting the same handful of problems.

  • Roofs, stucco and cooling equipment worn by the sun, which buyers deduct from their price.
  • Heirs living out of state who now own a Washington County house.
  • Second-home owners surprised by the full tax rate.
  • Crowding from new houses around Exit 13 and the Washington Fields area.
  • Unfinished or unpermitted work found during an inspection.

Start by pulling together the deed, your newest tax notice and permit records. Those three papers let a buyer or a title company see fast what could slow a closing.

sections.h2: Before you call for an offer
sections.html:
A call goes quicker when you can give the street address, the parcel number from your tax notice and an honest list of what is broken or worn out. Note any permits for a finished basement or addition. Tell us if the house is occupied, if a mortgage is still open, and who else is on the deed.

What follows is short. An offer arrives, you review it, and you decide. On a yes, the title company asks for payoff numbers, splits the property tax, files the deed with the county and drafts the closing papers.

faqs.q: Is Washington, UT the same as Washington County?
faqs.a: No. Washington is a city. Washington County also holds St. George, Hurricane and other communities. Tax bills and deeds for city properties go through county offices in St. George.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Washington, Utah?
faqs.a: November 30 each year. The Washington County Treasurer mails the notice, but you owe the bill even if it never reaches you. Ask the Treasurer's Office for a copy.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Washington County?
faqs.a: The Recorder charges $45.00 per document, plus $2.00 for each legal description over ten. Nothing is accepted after 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for work on my Washington house?
faqs.a: Usually yes for additions, basement finishes, pools, solar and detached buildings. Apply through the City Inspect portal run by the city's Building Department, or call (435) 656-6326.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Washington house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Houses sell in any condition, and a cash buyer who takes the house as-is lets you skip the repair bills.
